gen_risks.description: Sophisticated cyberattacks on state digital portals and core financial systems could disrupt critical PFM services and compromise sensitive government data.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an Information Security Management System (ISMS) based on ISO 27000, deploy a Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) and Security Operation Center (SOC), and institute a Business Continuity Management System.
gen_risks.evidence: Guatecompras and SICOIN stopped working, attributed to a cyber-attack.

gen_risks.description: Lack of transactional integration and limited interoperability between core IFMIS and peripheral PFM systems leads to data fragmentation and operational inefficiencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a PFM Integrated Conceptual Model, adopt enterprise architecture standards, and implement a dedicated interoperability platform for transactional data exchange.
gen_risks.evidence: System interoperability is limited to data transfers, with no transactional integration into the core financial systems.

gen_risks.description: Underdeveloped predictive analytics capabilities and lack of structured career paths for data professionals impede data-driven policymaking.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated data analytics units, operationalize innovation centers across MINFIN and SAT, and implement structured capacity-building and career development programs.
gen_risks.evidence: use of predictive analytics remains minimal... lack of structured career paths for data professionals

gen_risks.description: Exogenous economic shocks reducing remittance inflows could cause severe VAT revenue shortfalls, narrowing national fiscal space.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen medium-term fiscal frameworks (MTEF), improve risk assessment tools, and modernize revenue management systems to absorb fiscal volatility.
gen_risks.evidence: A decline in these inflows could considerably reduce Value-Added Tax collections, which account for 49 percent of government net income

gen_risks.description: Underfunded maintenance and weak lifecycle project monitoring result in public investment cost overruns and premature asset deterioration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a comprehensive project monitoring, evaluation, and closure framework that incorporates tools for estimating recurrent operation and maintenance costs.
gen_risks.evidence: underfunded maintenance, weak procurement competitiveness, lack of lifecycle project monitoring, and insufficient data on total costs and overruns.

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling legal conditions such as establishing the PIU and adopting the POM could block project effectiveness and disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize early drafting and adoption of the POM and expedite technical/fiduciary staffing for the PIU prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Category 1 until the Borrower has established the PIU, satisfactory to the Bank.

gen_risks.description: Complex, multi-system IT hardware and software modernization across core and peripheral PFM applications risks schedule slippage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute project deployment in phased, modular iterations, prioritizing essential budget execution modules before scaling peripheral platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: IFMIS reform projects tend to be costly and lengthy and should be realistically appraised

gen_risks.description: Low municipal adoption of the Gender-Based Budget Classifier (CPEG) limits visibility and accountability of subnational gender spending.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy upgraded local government financial management systems with automated gender tagging functionality and deliver targeted technical training to municipal staff.
gen_risks.evidence: only 112 municipalities out of 340 linked their budget to the CPEG

gen_risks.description: Fragmented presentation across public financial portals reduces citizen engagement and limits public oversight of government expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update the Fiscal Transparency Strategy, redesign web portals for improved user-centric usability, and institute full-cycle public consultations during budget formulation.
gen_risks.evidence: the fragmented presentation of portals reduces their visibility to the public.

gen_risks.description: Institutional instability and executive political turnover within implementing bodies risk eroding reform ownership and institutional momentum.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor implementation within the Technical Budget Directorate (DTP) under the oversight of joint governance bodies to sustain institutional commitment.
gen_risks.evidence: A common reason for the failure of PFM reforms in previous projects in Guatemala is the lack of adequate preparation and institutional stability

gen_risks.description: Extreme weather events, floods, and heatwaves could physically interrupt ICT infrastructure and cause service outages in PFM administrative operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy an ISO 22301-aligned Business Continuity Management System, enact a resilient cloud adoption strategy, and procure energy-efficient, climate-hardened ICT infrastructure.
gen_risks.evidence: increased heat waves and more frequent and intense extreme weather events... affect the capacity of systems that provide administrative services

gen_risks.description: Weak coordination between MINFIN and SEGEPLAN causes misalignment between multi-year public investment planning and annual budget allocations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize the Interinstitutional Committee to align SEGEPLAN's investment methodologies with MINFIN's PFM Integrated Conceptual Model and medium-term budget framework.
gen_risks.evidence: reliance on an annual budget framework limits medium-term planning and weakens coordination among planning, budgeting, and fiscal policy.

gen_risks.description: High staff turnover and technical human capital constraints impair the long-term maintenance and administration of digital PFM systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish permanent, structured capacity-building programs in PFM and data analytics to continually upskill personnel and mitigate talent loss.
gen_risks.evidence: Poor system maintenance, weak governance arrangements, human capital constraints... have left some existing PFM systems vulnerable and outdated.

gen_risks.description: Potential misalignment or duplication among donor-funded technical assistance programs (World Bank, IMF, IDB) reduces reform coherence.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain active, MINFIN-led donor coordination mechanisms to ensure seamless operational synergies across IMF, IDB, and World Bank workstreams.
gen_risks.evidence: The IMF is leading... The IDB is working... Together, these efforts form a cohesive agenda

gt_risks.description: Technical design risks are considered Substantial. PFM reforms typically require a whole-of-government approach and involve complex, cross-cutting changes that are often difficult to implement; these challenges are further amplified when reforms involve development or integration of sophisticated information systems. Many of the anticipated efficiency gains depend heavily on interoperability of processes and seamless integration of information systems across institutions, and the involvement of multiple stakeholders adds further complexity and increases the potential for misalignment or implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project design includes the development and application of well-defined, evidence-based PFM conceptual and governance models, informed by a diagnostic and reform strategy developed through stakeholder consultations, providing a clear and coherent framework expected to foster shared understanding, facilitate collaboration, and reduce fragmentation.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risks are Substantial. Given the complexity of PFM reforms, the project requires strong government commitment to ensure effective implementation and safeguard long-term sustainability. Since the project's beneficiaries extend beyond MINFIN, coordination challenges may arise during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: A PIU will be established within the Directorate of Public Treasury (DTP) for faster decision-making and improved coordination across MINFIN directorates. Component 3 will strengthen PIU operations (project management, financial management, procurement, monitoring, E&S risk management capacities); the Bank will provide training to the PIU and relevant stakeholders and facilitate change management mechanisms and a communications strategy. Coordination challenges involving multiple beneficiaries will be addressed through collaboration between MINFIN and SEGEPLAN via the Digital Transformation Commission.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks are Substantial. This is due to DTP's limited experience with donor-funded projects and lack of recent engagement with World Bank operations; DTP has no prior experience implementing the Bank's procurement regulations, and the low value of anticipated contracts may limit interest from international firms, reducing competition. DTP has basic financial management systems in place but its unfamiliarity with the Bank's FM policies and requirements may pose risks to achieving the PDO, potentially leading to delays in activity execution.
gt_risks.mitigation: Measures include setting up a PIU with qualified personnel, offering procurement training to PIU and DTP staff, conducting market analysis to find potential providers, and preparing a simplified Project Procurement Strategy for Development (PPSD).
